selectionPolicy: All 13 undispositioned objective 4.1 MCQs by existing triage priority then record ID; structural cues do not prove correctness or semantic error

questionProposals.assessedUnderstanding: Choose application-scoped management for personal-phone corporate apps without full-device enrolment; selective removal is not unique to MAM.
questionProposals.contentQualification: HOLD selective wipe as unique to MAM, MAM as supporting every app/platform without enrolment, or app policy as complete device protection. The explicit no-full-device-enrolment requirement disambiguates this current app-management choice; app support, corporate/personal account separation and command delivery still matter. Full-device management can offer selective removal too, and MDM/MAM can coexist. COPE/COBO name employer ownership/use, not app-management techniques for these personal phones. The captured older stem relied only on avoiding full wipe; current wording adds the narrower enrolment requirement and main removes personal-data immunity. Authored hard, captured easy and effective medium are uncalibrated labels. One app-control choice gives no independent ownership, identity, wipe completion or privacy evidence. No phone, enrolment, corporate account, policy or deletion executes.

questionProposals.assessedUnderstanding: Choose server-side permission checks for each requested object and action when a valid token still permits another user's private record; one authorisation fix.
questionProposals.contentQualification: HOLD valid tokens or OAuth metadata as automatically granting each object/action, checking one client-supplied user ID as complete authorisation, or token validation alone as a BOLA fix. Enforce server policy for the authenticated principal, tenant, requested object and operation; sharing/administrative roles may legitimately allow access beyond ownership, so owner-only equality is not a universal policy. Token scope/audience/lifetime and identity binding are separate requirements. Current single object-permission choice replaces snapshot compound API-function/BOLA/DoS wording and its token-prevents-BOLA/rate-limit-stops-DoS guarantees; no separate API-definition, authentication or rate-limit skill is assessed. Rate limits and opaque identifiers can complement controls but do not grant missing permission. Snapshot-only source, no authored substitute. Correlate prior m227 allowed-operation boundary; no API, token, identity, record request, cross-tenant read or successful fix is tested.

questionProposals.assessedUnderstanding: Choose the offered individual central-service enterprise wireless authentication exchange over shared credentials; encryption and trusted-server checks remain separate.
questionProposals.contentQualification: HOLD an Enterprise/802.1X/EAP/RADIUS label as specifying a secure EAP method, directory mapping, mutual authentication, modern wireless suite or verified server identity. EAP methods and client profiles determine credentials and server-certificate validation; 802.1X access authentication is distinct from wireless cipher/key-handshake behaviour and can also apply to wired networks. Personal-mode authentication can be cryptographically strong, but the offered shared-password/voucher/address models do not meet the stipulated individual central-service requirement. Current options replace the snapshot ambiguous Enterprise/group-master-key distractor with expressly shared Personal mode; current main removes assigning the wireless four-way handshake directly to 802.1X. This is one combined framework choice, not independent EAP, RADIUS, directory or session-key evidence. Generic WPA-Enterprise naming is not a recommendation of every historical WPA suite. Snapshot-only, hard to medium uncalibrated. No supplicant, AP, RADIUS exchange, certificate or key derivation is tested.

questionProposals.assessedUnderstanding: Recognise MDM as the offered enrolled-mobile configuration and remote-command platform; whole numbered naming scope and completed wipe remain held.
questionProposals.contentQualification: HOLD MDM naming as applied secure baselines, enrolment as proof of all required permissions/support, or sending a remote command as confirmed erasure. Supported operating systems, enrolment mode, connectivity and receipt/completion reporting govern actions; offline or failed commands leave data intact. UTM/NAC/XDR have different primary purposes but integrations can coexist, so product categories are not universally disjoint capabilities. Current stem bounds the target to enrolled corporate phones and requests commands, replacing authored all-device/encryption claims; three imported fallback corrections become specific contrasts. Imported QB1 question 23, domain 3 to 4 and medium to easy, uncalibrated. Hold whole 4.1 applied-technique scope for platform naming, retaining context without an alternate forced code. No device, baseline, encryption, management command or erasure occurs.

questionProposals.assessedUnderstanding: Choose enforced application control plus execution logging while preserving approved administration; one composite choice, not separate prevention/detection evidence.
questionProposals.contentQualification: HOLD an application-control label as a verified enforced allow policy, every unapproved script as wholly unable to run, or execution logging as blocking an attack. Interpreter/version/rule scope and allowed administrative paths matter; some enforcement constrains untrusted language features rather than rejecting every script. Audit mode alone is not the specified enforcement. Logs can be incomplete, disabled or unreviewed and need protected collection and response. Encoding can be legitimate or malicious, and representations vary; authentication/signatures do not prove safe code. Untested blanket removal risks required administration, without claiming removal can never be appropriate. Current generic enforcement/logging choice supersedes authored manually configured constrained-language/all-block-logging assertions and exclusive antivirus/patching contrasts. One composite decision has no separately scored prevention and detection components; strongly correlate m142 in one provisional family. No policy, PowerShell, encoded command, log or attack is executed.

questionProposals.assessedUnderstanding: Choose an enforced approved-script policy boundary over a bypassable shell preference; actual interpreter/rule coverage remains required.
questionProposals.contentQualification: HOLD every application-control product/rule as rejecting all unapproved scripts, signed/approved scripts as necessarily safe, or execution-policy configuration as a security boundary against determined users. Enforce the intended policy across actual interpreters, trusted paths and allowed language features; application-control modes can constrain rather than prohibit some untrusted script execution. Audit-only mode is not the requested enforcement. The current key removes authored AllSigned/RemoteSigned as prevention of malicious unsigned scripts and replaces it with the desired enforced policy; approved-signature decisions remain separate from code safety. Firewall and FDE serve other boundaries and can coexist, but do not determine local script permission in the stated running session. Logging remains useful teaching, not a separately assessed control. Authored domain 2 becomes effective 4. Strongly correlate m096; no rule, signer, Windows endpoint, shell preference, script or bypass is tested.

questionProposals.assessedUnderstanding: Choose an inactivity lock with reauthentication to reduce unattended-session exposure, retaining the pre-lock access window and manual-lock need.
questionProposals.contentQualification: HOLD automatic locking as instant protection at departure, a screen saver as necessarily an authentication lock, or reauthentication as revoking every session/token and blocking all remote access. The inactivity threshold leaves an access window and must fit operational/accessibility needs; manual lock remains necessary when leaving. A lock protects the local interactive session, not stolen credentials or every background service. Current single configuration choice replaces authored compound policy-violation/security-champion/compensating-control labelling; no independent administrative-policy, control-category or security-culture skill is assessed. Password lifetime and hidden shortcuts do not impose the requested idle-session barrier. Authored domain 1 to effective 4 and medium to easy are uncalibrated source changes. No workstation, idle timer, authentication, lock, background service or exposure is tested.
